content.text:
Yes—your PR fixes the exact bug reported in #219. It also handles several Gradle cases that #261 still gets wrong. However, I found a separate regression in yours that I would fix before merging.

I compared the current published commits: your `d8c0f1a7` and their `2ec6e8f1`, and ran regression tests against both.

The original issue is straightforward: `lib/build.gradle` exists, but `settings.gradle` includes only `:app`. Previously, search suggested:

```sh
./gradlew :lib:test --tests 'ATest'
```

Your PR correctly refuses that command. I confirmed the regression test fails on the pre-fix code and passes on yours. #261 also fixes this basic case.

The differences become clear with slightly more complex layouts:

| Case tested | Your #249 | Their #261 |
|---|---|---|
| `:lib` explicitly included | Correct command | Correct command |
| `:lib` undeclared; no root build file | Correctly declines | Correctly declines |
| Undeclared `:lib`, with root `build.gradle` | Correctly declines | Incorrectly suggests root `:test` |
| Undeclared child beneath declared `:parent` | Correctly declines | Incorrectly suggests `:parent:test` |
| Project renamed with `.name` or `.setName()` | Correctly declines | Emits the old project path |
| `modules/settings.gradle` includes `:core` | Correctly uses `-p modules :core:test` | Misses the valid command |
| Included `:lib` also contains its own wrapper | **Incorrectly selects root `:test`** | Correctly selects `:lib:test` |

These are executed command-derivation tests, not conclusions drawn only from PR descriptions.

1. **#261 leaves the parent-fallback problem unresolved.**

   Its Gradle helper returns `nil` for an undeclared project, but the surrounding discovery loop continues upward. With a root build file, the final VERIFY result becomes:

   ```sh
   ./gradlew :test --tests 'ATest'
   ```

   With a declared parent, it becomes:

   ```sh
   ./gradlew :parent:test --tests 'ATest'
   ```

   Neither establishes that the edited child is tested. Your `gradleBlocked` logic prevents this in both narrow and suite discovery. This is a substantive correctness improvement in your PR. See [#261’s ancestor walk](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/2ec6e8f1c06ce35f691b83211734dd952d8829a2/internal/sem/search_verify.go#L527).

2. **Your PR has a wrapper-location regression.**

   Consider a root settings file declaring `:lib`, with wrappers at both `gradlew` and `lib/gradlew`, but no `lib/settings.gradle`.

   Your resolver assumes that finding the wrapper beside `lib/build.gradle` makes `lib` a build root. It emits:

   ```sh
   cd lib && ./gradlew :test --tests 'ATest'
   ```

   But `:test` explicitly selects the root project’s task; the wrapper’s location does not establish a separate build. [Gradle documents this distinction](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/command_line_interface.html#sec:command_line_executing_tasks).

   The problematic shortcut is in [search_verify.go:711](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/entire-graph/fix-gradle-verify-project-membership-219/internal/sem/search_verify.go:711). My new regression test fails on yours and passes on both the original code and #261. The fix should determine the owning settings/build root independently of wrapper location.

3. **#261 also has a separate Rake bug.**

   Its new namespace scanner mishandles closing one namespace and opening another on the same line:

   ```ruby
   namespace :foo do
   end; namespace :bar do
     task :test
   end
   ```

   It derives `foo:test`. Real Rake lists `bar:test`, successfully runs it, and rejects `foo:test`. The scanner applies all openings before all closings, losing their order. See [the affected code](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/2ec6e8f1c06ce35f691b83211734dd952d8829a2/internal/sem/search_verify.go#L1754). This is unrelated to your Gradle work.

Your existing Gradle tests passed, and your full `go test ./internal/sem` passed in **162.680 seconds**. #261’s own new tests also passed; the additional comparison cases exposed its gaps. I did not execute real Gradle builds because this machine lacks a Java runtime. The Rake finding was checked against real Rake.

My recommendation is to retain your Gradle implementation, fix the wrapper-location regression, and reconcile #261’s overlapping Gradle changes separately from its Ruby, workspace-glob, and fixture changes. I would request changes on both current versions.

As for being ignored: [your PR](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/249) opened September 11; [#261](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/261) opened September 20 and also claims to close #219. There is clear duplication, and neither PR has a submitted review. That establishes overlap, but not whether the omission was intentional. Technically, your work does fix the issue and contains protections the later PR lacks.
